source_quote: One hour following a 24-hour cold shock, only 10 % of worms have regained any mobility; the remaining 90 % are either dead or immobile and dying
notes: Percent of worms mobile 1 h after return to 20 C following a 24 h cold shock at 2 C (nose-touch scoring); the remaining 90% were dead or immobile and dying. N = 150.

source_quote: Within 12 h of a 24-hour cold shock, virtually all worms are dead (Fig.
notes: Survival 12 h after return to 20 C following a 24 h cold shock at 2 C: described only as 'virtually all worms are dead'; the exact percentage exists only in Figure 1b, so response_value is null.

source_quote: One hour after a 12-hour cold shock, 95 % of worms are alive, though 35 % are immobile; however, fewer than 2 % are alive 24 h later.
notes: Survival 1 h after return to 20 C following a 12 h cold shock at 2 C; 35% of the survivors were immobile. N = 483.

source_quote: One hour after a 12-hour cold shock, 95 % of worms are alive, though 35 % are immobile; however, fewer than 2 % are alive 24 h later.
notes: Same 12 h cold shock scored 24 h after return to 20 C: the text gives only an upper bound ('fewer than 2 % are alive'), so response_value is left null.

source_quote: Two days after a 4-hour cold shock, approximately 60 % of the worms are still alive
notes: Survival 48 h after return to 20 C following a 4 h cold shock at 2 C. Value is stated as approximate. N = 166.

source_quote: By 96 h after a 4-hour cold shock, only 11 % of worms survive
notes: Survival 96 h after return to 20 C following a 4 h cold shock at 2 C. Almost all worms are alive 1 h after this cold shock, so the lethality is delayed ('phase two death').

source_quote: However, the population of wild-type worms stabilizes at approximately 20 % survival, while the population of fshr-1(ok778) mutants stabilizes at greater than 60 % survival
notes: Plateau survival of wild type after a 4 h cold shock at 2 C (very little further lethality after 72 h of recovery). Stated as approximate; note the 96 h figure of 11% reported elsewhere in the same paper for the same condition.

source_quote: However, the population of wild-type worms stabilizes at approximately 20 % survival, while the population of fshr-1(ok778) mutants stabilizes at greater than 60 % survival
notes: Plateau survival of fshr-1(ok778) null mutants after a 4 h cold shock at 2 C is given only as a lower bound ('greater than 60 %'), so response_value is null. Mutants are more cold-shock resistant than wild type (p < 0.0001 at all time points except 1 h). N = 150.

source_quote: All mutant worms are still alive at the end of the cold-shock, and more than 85 % are mobile.
notes: Percent mobile immediately after a 12 h cold shock at 2 C in fshr-1(ok778) mutants; given only as a lower bound ('more than 85 %'), so response_value is null. Wild-type worms die within 24 h of the same treatment. N = 379.
